keyframe_review.note: 28,591 km2. Cliopatria's shape (28,600-34,900 km2, 9.9-14.3E, 50.0-52.0N) contains Meissen, Weimar, Orlamunde and Eisenach and none of Dessau, Bernburg, Kothen, Zerbst or Wittenberg; it is the Wettin lands (Margraviate of Meissen and Landgraviate of Thuringia, which the Wettins inherited in 1263), and Cliopatria's Electorate of Saxony row resumes in 1487 with the same bounding box. Only the Weimar-Orlamunde part is Ascanian, and only until 1344 (Orlamunde sold to the Wettins on 25 April 1344) and 1372 (Weimar annexed by the Wettins after Herman VI died); the table's 'Weimar-Orlamunde (until 1486)' marks the span of the line, not land held (repair after review). The Ascanian lands of 1260 are Anhalt (2,300 km2 for the later duchy, per the Principality of Anhalt page), Saxe-Wittenberg and Lauenburg (the Duchy of Saxony of John I and Albert II, who 'ruled jointly' from 1260), and Weimar-Orlamunde. The Ascanian Margraviate of Brandenburg (to 1320) is drawn by the margraviate-of-brandenburg row, not here.

ledger.note: 1260: after the death of Albert I of Saxony his sons John I and Albert II rule the Ascanian lands jointly. 'In 1260, Albert I's sons Albert II and John I succeeded their father' (Saxe-Lauenburg) and 'ruled jointly' (Saxe-Wittenberg); Albert I died on 7 October 1260 (House of Ascania). Cliopatria's row begins in 1260; the house is older (Esico, Count of Ballenstedt, 1036). The region is the dynasty's lands outside Brandenburg as read from the pages, not Cliopatria's shape.

region.text: Anhalt, the Duchy of Saxony of John I and Albert II, Weimar-Orlamunde

ledger.note: 20 September 1296: the Duchy of Saxony is partitioned into Saxe-Wittenberg and Saxe-Lauenburg. 'Who by 1296 definitely partitioned Saxony, providing Saxe-Lauenburg for the brothers' (Saxe-Lauenburg); before 20 September 1296 'the definite partitioning of the Duchy of Saxony' (Saxe-Wittenberg). Both lines are Ascanian: one state, one colour. In 1303 Lauenburg is divided again into shares.
1307: the Askanier acquire the lordship of Zerbst from the lords of Barby (paraphrased; the page gives the year, not the extent of the lordship).

1315: the Aschersleben line dies out and its district passes to the Bishopric of Halberstadt, splitting Anhalt-Bernburg in two (Principality of Anhalt: 'annexed by the Bishopric of Halberstadt'). Page wording: 'The family ruling in Aschersleben became extinct in 1315, and this district was subsequently incorporated in the neighboring Bishopric of Halberstadt.' The counterpart is the prince-bishopric (slug prince-bishopric-of-halberstadt), which needs a dossier.

25 April 1344: the counts of Weimar-Orlamunde sell Orlamunde to the Wettins: 'Orlamünde was sold to the Wettins on April 25, 1344.' (House of Ascania; 'In 1354, Orlamunde was annexed to the House of Wettin, and the family changed seat to Schauenforst'). The Thuringian Counts' War page (1342-1346) says nothing of a sale of Orlamunde; it says the war ended the counts' imperial immediacy and made their main territories Wettin fiefs.

region.text: Orlamunde, sold to the Wettins on 25 April 1344

ledger.note: 1356: the Golden Bull gives Rudolph I of Saxe-Wittenberg the Saxon electoral dignity (he 'exclusively received the Saxon electoral dignity'); Saxe-Wittenberg then came to be known as the Electorate of Saxony. Saxe-Lauenburg also claimed it (1314 double election). The land is drawn by the Electorate of Saxony row from 1363.

1363: the Ascanian electorate of Saxe-Wittenberg passes to Cliopatria's Electorate of Saxony row (starts 1363; the page dates the dignity to 1356). Bridging entry so that the land is drawn once. The Duchy of Saxe-Wittenberg page (re-read in the repair) dates the electoral dignity to 1356 and gives no 1363; 1363 is only where Cliopatria's Electorate of Saxony row starts. The dynasty's holdings outside that row (Anhalt, Lauenburg, Weimar, Luneburg) stay in this dossier.

ledger.note: 1370: 'In the same year, the Principality of Lüneburg was granted to Albrecht and Wenceslaus I' of the Saxe-Wittenberg line (House of Ascania; its table: 'Luneburg (until 1388)'). The War of the Lüneburg Succession page, opened in the repair, dates Charles IV's enfeoffment of Albert, Rudolf and Wenceslas to 1369, the homage of the towns of Luneburg and Hanover to January 1371, and the Welfs keep Celle, so the dossier keeps the Ascanian page's year and a reading of the extent (50 km at Luneburg, 15 km at Hanover). Why this stays here and not in electorate-of-saxony: the grant was to the Saxe-Wittenberg dukes, whose home land electorate-of-saxony draws from 1363, but Cliopatria's Electorate of Saxony row (5,458 km2 at Wittenberg, 1363-1428) holds no Luneburg cell, so that dossier has no shape to attach it to; it is drawn once, here, under the dynasty. If the electorate's dossier takes Luneburg, drop this gain, the 1388 loss and the Luneburg and Hanover discs of the 1370 and 1373 keyframes.

ledger.note: 1372: Herman VI, the last count of Weimar of the line, dies and the Wettins annex Weimar: 'After Herman's death Weimar was annexed to the House of Wettin.' (House of Ascania; its table: Herman VI reign '25 July 1365 - 1372', died 1372, the year from the table, not from the prose). The Thuringian Counts' War page says that after the war of 1342-1346 the counts held their main territories as Wettin fiefs and 'Weimar fell to Wettin as an agreed fief', so the counts' tenure may have been a fief from c.1346; the dossier follows the Ascanian page for the annexation.

ledger.note: 1388: 'The Ascanians were replaced in 1388 by Albrecht's stepsons from the House of Welf' (House of Ascania). The War of the Lüneburg Succession page: Henry won the Battle of Winsen an der Aller on 28 May 1388, Wenceslas died soon after, and the inheritance agreement of 1389 left 'the Principality ... finally secured for the Welfs'.

region.text: the Principality of Luneburg, until 1388 (with the town of Hanover)

ledger.note: 1468: 'The last prince of the original line of Anhalt-Bernburg died in 1468' and 'his lands were inherited by the princes of the sole remaining line, that of Anhalt-Zerbst' (Principality of Anhalt prose; the page's table says instead that 'Bernburg was inherited by Anhalt-Dessau line', and the page has George I partition Zerbst into Zerbst and Dessau after acquiring Bernburg). Internal to the house.
1473: after Adolph's death Valdemar VI and Albert VI of the Dessau line take over Kothen under the succession contract of 1471 (paraphrased). Internal to the house.

1486: Cliopatria's House of Ascania row ends. The year is the House of Ascania table's 'Weimar-Orlamünde (until 1486)', which gives the span of that line; it is not land held, because the same page has the Wettins take Orlamunde in 1344 and Weimar in 1372 and says 'By 1467, the Ascanians no longer held any possessions, as the Wettins took over everything' (a sentence that sits oddly with Anhalt and Saxe-Lauenburg, which the same page carries on). The house does not end: Anhalt continues to 1918 and Saxe-Lauenburg to 1689 (the page: 'The Saxe-Lauenburg line ended with Julius Francis in 1689'). The dissolve is a bridging entry set by Cliopatria's row; the land passes to the successors principality-of-anhalt and duchy-of-saxe-lauenburg.

notes:
Cliopatria's House of Ascania row (1260-1486, 12 shapes of 28,600-34,900 km2) is mislabelled: the shape is the Wettin land of Meissen and Thuringia (no Anhalt, Wittenberg, Bernburg, Kothen or Zerbst cells; the same bounding box as the Electorate of Saxony row of 1487-1805; the Wettins inherited Thuringia in 1263 and received the Electorate in 1423). All 12 shapes are marked wrong. The corrected state is the Ascanian lands outside Brandenburg: Anhalt, Saxe-Wittenberg (1260-1362; from 1363 Cliopatria's Electorate of Saxony row draws it), Saxe-Lauenburg, Luneburg 1370-1387 and the counts of Weimar-Orlamunde (Orlamunde to 1343, Weimar to 1372). The discs around the towns are approximations of principalities whose extent no page gives (Anhalt: 2,300 km2 for the later duchy).

Not in the dossier: (1) the Ascanian Margraviate of Brandenburg 1260-1320 (the House of Ascania page: 'the Brandenburg line became extinct in 1320'; Louis IV gave Brandenburg to his son in 1323; Rudolph I of Saxe-Wittenberg 'failed with his claims to Brandenburg'), which belongs to margraviate-of-brandenburg; (2) the Bergedorf and Vierlande lands that Eric III of Saxe-Lauenburg pawned to Lubeck in 1370, that his sons seized back in 1401 and that were ceded to Hamburg and Lubeck at Perleberg on 23 August 1420 (Saxe-Lauenburg page), too small for the grid and left out of the shape; (3) the extent of the Weimar and Orlamunde counties: their own page would not load (three titles tried). The House of Ascania page has Orlamunde sold to the Wettins on 25 April 1344 (annexed 1354) and Weimar annexed after Herman VI's death (1372); the Thuringian Counts' War page (opened in the repair) says the counts' main territories became Wettin fiefs after the war of 1342-1346 and gives no figures, so the 15 km and 20 km discs stay approximate. The table's 'Weimar-Orlamünde (until 1486)' is the span of the line, not land held; the 1486 dissolve is a bridging entry (confidence 1); (4) Anhalt, Saxe-Lauenburg and Saxe-Wittenberg after the dates of the row.

The row ends in 1486 because Cliopatria's data does; the house continues (Anhalt, Saxe-Lauenburg). The successors principality-of-anhalt and duchy-of-saxe-lauenburg have no dossier yet; without them the Ascanian lands drop off the map in 1487. Page budget: 5 pages used. Pages disagree: the 1252 partition produced Aschersleben, Bernburg and Zerbst lines (Principality of Anhalt) or Aschersleben, Bernburg and Kothen (House of Ascania). No ruler strip: the pages give a table of lines, not one list. Gazetteer names used that it may lack: Bernburg, Koethen, Dessau, Aschersleben, Zerbst, Ratzeburg, Lauenburg, Luneburg, Orlamuende. Repair after review (2026-10-25): added the loss of Orlamunde to the Wettins (25 April 1344) and of Weimar (1372) with keyframes 1344-1362 and 1373-1387, and removed the Weimar and Orlamunde discs after those years; Luneburg stays in this dossier (no Cliopatria shape of electorate-of-saxony holds it; see the 1370 gain) and now includes the town of Hanover (homage of January 1371), with counterpart principality-of-luneburg; Aschersleben's counterpart is prince-bishopric-of-halberstadt; the 1468 heirs are quoted from the Principality of Anhalt page, which names Anhalt-Zerbst in prose and Anhalt-Dessau in its table. Disagreements kept: the War of the Lüneburg Succession page dates the enfeoffment to 1369 and the House of Ascania page to 1370 (the dossier keeps 1370, the page of the table); the Thuringian Counts' War page has Weimar a Wettin fief soon after 1346 whereas the House of Ascania page has it annexed after 1372.
